headings: # A11YRepair: Bridging Web Accessibility Barriers via Knowledge-Enhanced Divide-and-Conquer Repair
#A11yDev: understanding contemporary software accessibility practices from twitter conversations.
limitations:
## 7. Threats to Validity

Data Leakage.
Unlike many APR benchmarks that derive tasks from GitHub pull request histories (Just et al., 2014; Jimenez et al., 2024; Yang et al., 2025b),
which risks exposing ground-truth fixes during LLM training.
A11YBench is constructed from violations detected by the A11Y Checker.
This design avoids leaking the ground truth fixes into model pretraining corpora.

Weak Oracles.
A11Y checkers
may introduce false positives, so provide weak repair oracles to threaten the validity.
We mitigate this risk by using IBM A11Y Checker (IBM, 2025c), which offers good reported precision (97.5%) and highest recall among rule-based checkers (He et al., 2025).
Importantly, the manual audit, low silent regression count, and real-world PR acceptance collectively provide independent validation signals beyond the single checker. The empirical evidence suggests that improvements are not merely checker-specific artifacts.

## 8. Related Work

Automated Program Repair.
Traditional work including search-based (Le Goues et al., 2012), constraint-based (Nguyen et al., 2013), and template-based methods (Liu et al., 2019) have recently evolved toward LLM-driven systems (Huang et al., 2024b; Yang et al., 2025a; Zhang et al., 2024a).
For example, AlphaRepair (Xia and Zhang, 2022), ChatRepair (Xia and Zhang, 2024), and Gamma (Zhang et al., 2023a) demonstrate how pretrained knowledge can yield human-like fixes.
Especially, recent efforts explore autonomous repair agents (Bouzenia et al., 2025; Yang et al., 2024; Xia et al., 2025b; Wang et al., 2025; Zhang et al., 2024b; Ruan et al., 2025; Meng et al., 2024; Team et al., 2025; Ye et al., 2025; Chen et al., 2025).
These systems mimic human debugging to implement the repair workflow.
Unlike the general purpose repair systems, A11YRepair is the first repo-level web A11Y repair tool.

Web Accessibility Detection.
Web A11Y detection (Tafreshipour et al., 2024; Chiou et al., 2024; Chiou et al., 2021; Jain et al., 2025)
follows standards such as WCAG (WAI, 2025e).
These guidelines enabled the development of checkers (IBM, 2025c; WebAIM, 2025b; Systems, 2025; Google, 2025).
While effective for syntactic or layout violations, static checkers struggle with semantic issues, e.g., whether an image’s alt text
reflects its visual content.
Recent work (He et al., 2025; Fathallah et al., 2025)
leverage LLMs to identify semantic issues.
These advances
provide a foundation
for our study: A11YRepair addresses the remaining challenge by
turning
detected violations into actionable
fixes for the end-to-end accessible web development.

Web Accessibility Correction.
Early work relied on rule-based HTML/DOM transformations (Almasoud and Mathkour, 2019; Ferati and Sulejmani, 2016) or expert-in-the-loop methods (Mangiatordi and Lazzari, 2018; Seixas Pereira et al., 2024), while others addressed specific violations using computer vision, such as alt-text generation (Wu et al., 2017).
